h1: Window cleaning in Lakeside at North Lakeway
intro: Lakeside at North Lakeway is a small neighborhood of newer, larger homes on the north side of Lakeway. CleanzATX cleans windows here and the bigger glass fits our pure water poles well.

sections.h2: What Lakeside at North Lakeway homes are like
paragraphs: The subdivision is small, with newer homes between 2,700 and 4,350 square feet. Prices run from $800K to $1.1M. There is no gate and no HOA, so each home sets its own schedule. It sits on the north side of the city, beside other North Lakeway neighborhoods.

Homes of this size usually have two stories, wide front elevations and plenty of windows on the back. Many have covered patios with large glass doors. With that much glass, the homes can look a lot better or a lot worse depending on its condition.

sections.h2: What Lakeside at North Lakeway windows deal with
paragraphs: Newer neighborhoods on the edge of town see construction dust more often. Wind brings it onto the glass and it sticks when morning dew arrives. Lawns that are still establishing get heavy watering, and that spray reaches windows near the ground. Mineral spots form fast on fresh sod days.

Pollen is the seasonal problem: cedar from December to February and live oak in March and April. Glass on the west side holds afternoon heat, which bakes spots into the surface. Pure water at near 0 TDS rinses clean, and hard water spot removal costs $10 per pane.

sections.h2: How we work Lakeside at North Lakeway
paragraphs: Scheduling is easy because there is no gate or HOA to contact. We pull into the driveway and run poles from the ground to reach second story windows. Inside work uses squeegees and hand drying, with drop cloths on the floor. For a home this size, we usually pair windows with a house soft wash, or a patio cleaning by hand so nothing gets soaked.

A 3,500 square foot home costs about $350 for exterior windows at $0.10 per square foot, which is our typical job. Count on about three hours outside and one hour and 45 minutes inside. The minimum job is $200.

faq.q: Do you clean newer homes with big sliders?
faq.a: Yes. Large sliding doors are common here, and pure water dries them without streaks. We clean tracks at $5 when you want them done.

faq.q: Why do my windows look dirty so soon after cleaning?
faq.a: New construction nearby sends dust into the air. Plans on a shorter cycle, such as Quarterly or Every 2 Months, keep the glass clear between big dust days.

faq.q: What does a 3,500 square foot house cost?
faq.a: About $350 for exterior windows. Both sides run $15 per window, and screens add $5 each. Roof and house soft wash start at $0.25 and $0.20 per square foot.

faq.q: Can you do the back patio?
faq.a: Yes. Patios are cleaned by hand so they do not get soaked, and flatwork runs $0.18 per square foot for concrete, with a $250 minimum.
